parameters.text:
<Low, flat Northern soldier; restrained gratitude, no ceremony. Mood: idle.> The ford first. I have too few guards to bury another.
<long pause>
<Low, flat Northern soldier; restrained gratitude, no ceremony. Mood: idle.> The bridge cost us enough. Now a grey bear takes goats from the pens. The boy got out; Maud has him by her fire. The cave mouth is below her hut on the burned bank. Will you put an end to this?
<long pause>
<Low, flat Northern soldier; restrained gratitude, no ceremony. Mood: idle.> Bring the ember-claw back. Sixty gold and a fitted trinket each. I will keep gifts for anyone away. Go carefully; that bear has lived through more winters than this Watch.
<long pause>
<Low, flat Northern soldier; restrained gratitude, no ceremony. Mood: idle.> Then take the time. Cold courage does nobody any good.
<long pause>
<Low, flat Northern soldier; restrained gratitude, no ceremony. Mood: idle.> Below Maud’s hut. Follow the miners’ track. Come back with the claw, and with every soul you take in.
<long pause>
<Low, flat Northern soldier; restrained gratitude, no ceremony. Mood: idle.> Still warm. Tobin can work with this. Your gold is counted, and there is a rare trinket fitted to each of your callings. Accepting replaces any trinket you already wear. Shall I present them?
<long pause>
<Low, flat Northern soldier; restrained gratitude, no ceremony. Mood: idle.> They will stay here. A promise does not spoil overnight.
<long pause>
<Low, flat Northern soldier; restrained gratitude, no ceremony. Mood: idle.> For the ones here, and the ones we expect home. The Watch remembers who stood for this town.
<long pause>
<Low, flat Northern soldier; restrained gratitude, no ceremony. Mood: idle.> The pens are quiet. The boy is home. That is enough good news for one day.
